original_question: Let G be an extension of a normal elementary abelian subgroup A by an elementary abelian group B ≅ G/A such that A contains an element a with C_B(a) = 1. Is it true that the rank of the subgroup Z(⟨a, B⟩) ∩ (⟨a, B⟩)′ is at most the rank of B?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.150 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of Unsolved Problems in Group Theory. The Kourovka Notebook, on p. 182. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right open problem and preserves its core structure: a group built from a normal elementary abelian subgroup A and an elementary abelian B with B ≅ G/A, an element a ∈ A with trivial centralizer in B, and the proposed inequality comparing the rank of a central commutator-type subgroup with rank(B). ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, B should be presented as an actual subgroup/complement of G, equivalently G = A ⋊ B with A normal, so that both C_B(a) and ⟨a,B⟩ are unambiguous.
The notation should be spelled out: C_B(a) is the centralizer of a in B, Z(H) is the center of H, and H' is the derived subgroup of H.

The word "rank" should be defined explicitly here as the vector-space dimension of an elementary abelian group over its prime field (equivalently, the minimal number of generators in the finite case).

A paper-faithful stand-alone version should not add assumptions not stated in the problem, such as finiteness, a common prime for A and B, or any nilpotency hypothesis. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let G = A ⋊ B, where A is a normal elementary abelian subgroup and B is an elementary abelian subgroup with B ≅ G/A. Assume that A contains an element a such that C_B(a) = 1. If H = ⟨a,B⟩, must one have rank(Z(H) ∩ H') ≤ rank(B), where Z(H) denotes the center of H, H' its derived subgroup, and rank means the dimension of an elementary abelian group over its prime field?
justification: This arXiv item is the Kourovka Notebook, so the relevant target is an open problem rather than a numbered conjecture or theorem. The draft is already very close to the official formulation of Problem 21.150; the main sharpening needed is only to make the subgroup/complement role of B explicit and to unpack the notation so the question can stand alone without relying on surrounding group-theoretic conventions. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
